verdict.rationale: Pandoc's documented core is conversion between word-processing and markup formats such as docx, HTML and LaTeX. Hands-on reports show structure such as headings and tables carried into Word with real styles. Other reports say fidelity is limited: its internal representation is less expressive than source or target formats, tables broke or misaligned in PDF, characters were silently dropped, and docx reference docs supply only styles, with table autofit needing workarounds. missing for 10: a first-party claim or documentation of layout/font/image preservation, reliable table fidelity across outputs, page-layout control, independent corroboration of high-fidelity round trips.

support.subject: As a power user, document conversion preserves layout, fonts, images, and tables rather than flattening them

citations.quote: Pandoc can convert between numerous markup and word processing formats, including, but not limited to, various flavors of Markdown, HTML, LaTeX and Word docx.
Pandoc is the only one that consistently maps Markdown headers to real Word styles rather than just bigger fonts.
scripts wrote model inputs as Markdown tables embedded in a Markdown writeup, and Pandoc produced the Word report for sponsors.
